objective: Determine whether official county-scale absence or eradication statements can support a bounded verified-absent lane without converting source omission, survey non-detection, local eradication, or regulatory status into county absence.

policy.verifiedAbsentRequirement: An authoritative source must explicitly identify the exact taxon, exact county, defined time, and county-scale absence or eradication scope.
neverSufficientAlone: species omitted from a list or map
policy.presenceCompatibility: A later or otherwise controlling presence record remains compatible with historical eradication evidence and controls the public compatibility determination.

sourceInventory.authority: County of Monterey Agricultural Commissioner's Office
sourceInventory.reason: The official page explicitly labels named weeds as eradicated from Monterey County and supplies eradication histories. Dated county crop reports independently preserve historical eradication statements for a subset of the taxa.

taxa.reason: No active Project Isitusa catalog species resolves exactly.
The page title text and linked current profile use different taxon identities; negative evidence cannot rely on a convenient synonym inference.
The current page labels the taxon eradicated from the county, but the inspected history does not expose a dated county-status statement suitable for a frozen temporal scope.

The current official county page labels Hydrilla eradicated and describes subsequent negative surveys; the 2015 county crop report states that Hydrilla has been eradicated. A bounded review must freeze the historical date, county scope, and later-presence conflict check before any assertion.
The source-to-catalog identity is not exact, and the same page warns that an undetected infestation might exist.

The current official county page labels diffuse knapweed eradicated and describes a declaration after several years of negative surveys; the 2005 county crop report states that it has been eradicated. A bounded review must freeze the historical date, county scope, and later-presence conflict check before any assertion.

sourceInventory.authority: USDA APHIS Federal Register rule, 64 FR 48245
sourceInventory.reason: The rule explicitly concerns a quarantined portion of Orange County. Eradication from that bounded regulatory area cannot establish absence from the entire county pair.

sourceInventory.authority: Boulder County Parks and Open Space
sourceInventory.reason: Eradication of the only known population is an inventory-qualified local eradication statement, not an explicit assertion that the species is absent throughout the county.

sourceInventory.observedScope: Approximately 1,200 sentinel traps across five named wine-grape pest targets.
sourceInventory.reason: The official page says the named pests have not been found, but the result is surveillance non-detection and the page does not allocate dated target-specific effort sufficient for a county absence assertion.

The page describes systematic searches and says listed pests are not known to occur currently. A knowledge-state statement is not an explicit county absence determination and lacks target-specific dated effort.

sourceInventory.authority: USGS Nonindigenous Aquatic Species, citing New Hampshire Department of Environmental Services
sourceInventory.reason: The eradication status is attached to a Lake Sunapee locality record, not the whole county, and the species is not currently resolved in the Project Isitusa catalog.

sourceInventory.authority: King County Department of Natural Resources and Parks
sourceInventory.reason: A non-active record may mean controlled, eradicated, under observation, or no active growth. The source explicitly warns that statuses change with fieldwork and reports; neither closed nor inactive can be promoted to county absence.

sourceInventory.authority: USDA APHIS federal quarantine status layer and linked regulatory documents
sourceInventory.reason: A rescinded quarantine can reflect regulatory or operational criteria and does not by itself state that the exact species is absent from the exact county.

findings.conclusion: County-scale verified absence is realistically obtainable only as sparse, source-specific manual authoritative evidence. No national automated county-absence source was established. Zero verified-absent remains the honest current projection.

requiredFields: direct source URL and retained bytes
exact source and catalog scientific names
explicit county name resolved to county FIPS
defined historical or current time scope
stopConditions: The retained source does not explicitly state county-scale absence or eradication.
The source statement is undated and no defensible historical time scope can be frozen.
The source taxon differs from the catalog target without an authoritative exact mapping.
The source describes only a site, waterbody, regulatory area, known population, or survey footprint.
The source contains an unresolved caveat suggesting an undetected county infestation.
Independent review or later-presence conflict screening is incomplete.

release.reason: This is a source-discovery evaluation only. It creates no evidence assertion, determination, generated projection, or public release.

nextAction: Freeze a maximum-two-pair manual-authoritative pilot for Monterey County Hydrilla and diffuse knapweed only after dated source bytes, exact county scope, independent review, and later-presence conflict checks are all reproducible.
